gaps.sentence: He denied everything ___ the face of the evidence.
gaps.hint: ___ the face of = when confronted with
gaps.explanation: 'in the face of' = despite / when confronted by.

gaps.sentence: The soldiers were ___ of danger once they had crossed the river.
gaps.explanation: 'Out of danger' = no longer at risk.

gaps.sentence: The 8:15 train left ___ time, to the second.
The new hall is ___ far the largest building on campus.
gaps.explanation: 'By far' strengthens a superlative: by far the largest.

gaps.sentence: The firm was put ___ liquidation by the end of March.
gaps.explanation: 'Put into liquidation' — the formal process of closing a company.'

gaps.sentence: He stayed ___ touch with every colleague he'd ever had.
I did it ___ my own initiative — nobody asked me.
gaps.explanation: 'of one's own initiative' = without being asked.

gaps.sentence: The letter arrived ___ due course — three weeks later.
gaps.hint: ___ due course = at the expected time
gaps.explanation: 'in due course' = at the proper time eventually.
